lines.en: Hi, I’m Andre. **Are you ready to order?**
lines.pt: Oi, eu sou o Andre. Vocês já podem pedir?

lines.en: The chicken is great. **It comes with** rice and salad.
lines.pt: O frango é ótimo. Vem com arroz e salada.
Legal! Eu vou querer o frango, por favor.

lines.en: Great. Would you like something to drink?
lines.pt: Ótimo. Gostaria de algo para beber?

lines.en: **Could we have** two waters? My friend is late.
lines.pt: Podemos pedir duas águas? Minha amiga está atrasada.

lines.en: Sure! I’ll bring them now. **Enjoy your meal** later!
lines.pt: Claro! Já trago. Bom apetite mais tarde!

lines.en: Thank you, Andre. **Could we have** one more menu?
lines.pt: Obrigada, Andre. Podemos ter mais um cardápio?

pages.title: Ordering in a Restaurant

unit.name: Eating out & shopping
map: Asking for the bill and paying

situation.text: You sit down in a restaurant in the United States. A waiter comes to your table. You ask for advice, order food and drinks, and ask for one extra thing.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can talk to a waiter: ask for a recommendation, order a dish and a drink, and ask for something extra — politely.
canDo: Ask for things for the table: Could we have…?
Understand: Are you ready to order?
success: I order food and a drink.
I ask for one extra thing.
pages.think: In Brazil, how do you call the waiter? How is it different in English?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: sentar numa mesa e falar com o garçom.
solo: Peça que o estudante descreva a última vez que comeu fora.
Leia o objetivo e os 4 critérios de sucesso.
group: Cada estudante diz uma comida que pediria num restaurante.
Mostre os critérios: serão a missão da aula.
extra: Do you like eating out?
What is your favorite restaurant?
support: Aceite respostas curtas e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Ask real questions about food and the student’s week.
intro.group: One question per student; then ask a classmate the same question.

pages.recall: Unit 2 (daily life): “I usually…”. Ask: What do you usually eat for lunch?
pages.tip: Collect food words from the answers: you will use them in the dialogue.

teach.goal: Entrar no inglês e levantar vocabulário de comida.
extra: What is your favorite dish?
Who cooks at your house?

errors.r: I like pizza very much. / I really like pizza.

support: Mostre os chips de resposta e peça que escolham um.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Restaurants in the USA have some habits that surprise visitors. Look, guess, then read.

cards.pt: O garçom se apresenta pelo nome.
cards.note: “Hi, I’m Andre. I’ll be your server.” He will come back to your table many times.
Servers earn a low base pay, so most people leave 15–20% of the bill.

cards.pt: A água da casa costuma ser grátis.
cards.note: Many restaurants bring tap water with ice. You can say “Just water, please.”

qs.q: What does the server do at the start?
qs.pt: O que o garçom faz no começo?

levels.A2: He says his name and asks about drinks.
levels.B1: He introduces himself and tells you he will be your server.
levels.B2: He introduces himself, which makes the service feel personal, and takes your drink order first.

qs.q: Why do people leave a tip?
qs.pt: Por que as pessoas deixam gorjeta?

levels.A2: Servers do not earn much money from the restaurant.
levels.B1: A tip is a big part of a server’s pay, so leaving one is expected.
levels.B2: Tipping is part of the system: the base pay is low, so a tip of 15–20% is the norm for good service.

qs.q: What can you ask if you don’t know what to order?
qs.pt: O que perguntar se você não sabe o que pedir?

levels.A2: What do you recommend? Is it good?
levels.B1: What do you recommend? What comes with it?
levels.B2: What would you recommend for someone who doesn’t eat meat?

pages.compare: In Brazil the service charge (10%) is often already on the bill. In the USA the tip is usually your decision at the end. What is it like in your city?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural: garçom com nome, gorjeta, água grátis.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Compare com o “serviço 10%” do Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
answers: Q2: tip = parte importante do pagamento do garçom (15–20%).
extra: Do you leave a tip in your country?
Would you like to ask the waiter for advice?
support: Use as respostas A1 como andaime.
stretch: B2: discuta prós e contras do sistema de gorjeta.

teach.goal: Entender a cena e depois 4 informações.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: onde estão?
2ª escuta: prato, acompanhamento, bebida e motivo.
group: Duplas anotam antes de revelar.
answers: Pass 2: chicken · rice (and salad) · water · her friend is late.
extra: Who is the waiter? Who is the guest?
Is the guest in a hurry?

qs.q: What does the guest ask first?
What does she ask for to drink?
Why does she want one more menu?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê a hóspede; você lê o garçom; troquem.
Peça o reconto.
group: Leitura em pares e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia.
answers: recommend · chicken · two waters · a friend is coming
extra: What would YOU order?
What would you ask the waiter?

errors.r: Could we have two waters, please?

support: Mostre a tradução (PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: The server asks if you can order now.
Ask the server for a good dish.
Order food or a drink. Very natural.
Ask for something extra for the table.
Say what is on the plate.
The server says it when the food arrives.
You need more time to choose.

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others help you understand the waiter.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes do significado.
Compare I’ll have × I’d like.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria.
answers: Server asks · Asking for advice · Ordering · Asking for extras · Server asks
extra: Which one is for a friendly restaurant?
Which one is for a fancy restaurant?

errors.r: I’ll have the soup. / I’d like the soup.

patterns.name: Ordering
ex: I’ll have the soup and a salad.

patterns.name: Asking for things at the table
ex: Could we have the menu, please?
Could we have some more bread?

patterns.name: Asking for advice
ex: What do you recommend for lunch?
What do you recommend, the fish or the pasta?

patterns.name: Describing a dish
ex: It comes with fries and a salad.

swap.tpt: Eu vou querer {dish} e {drink}, por favor.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: I would like to order the soup.
We would like two glasses of water, please.
Yes, that will be all, thank you.
register.note: Both are polite. Spoken English is shorter and uses contractions.

teach.goal: Fixar 2 padrões principais: I’ll have… e Could we have…? Os outros são expansão.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo.
Use “Swap the words”: o estudante fala a frase completa.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 e 04 são expansão.
extra: Order for two people: I’ll have… and my friend will have…
Ask for one extra thing for the table.

errors.w: I will to have the soup.

support: Só o padrão I’ll have… na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine: What do you recommend? → I’ll have that.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In English the important words are stronger and longer. “I’ll HAVE the CHICKen.” The small words are quick and weak.

own.prompt: Write your own order with “I’ll have…”. Mark the strong words.
own.criteria: Clap on the strong words. Do the small words sound quick?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: ênfase na frase (palavras fortes e fracas).
solo: Modele devagar e normal; o estudante bate palmas nas sílabas fortes.
Depois usa com o pedido dele.
group: Coro, depois duplas.
Cada estudante cria um pedido e marca as palavras fortes.
answers: Identify 1: I’ll have the CHICKen. · Identify 2: What do you recomMEND?

errors.w: Todas as palavras com a mesma força
errors.r: Palavras de conteúdo fortes, palavras pequenas fracas

support: Conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You don’t know what to order. What do you ask?
items.why: What do you recommend? asks for advice.

items.q: 2. You want the soup. What do you say?
items.why: I’ll have + dish is the natural order.

items.q: 3. You want some bread for the table.
items.why: Could we have… is polite for the table.

items.q: 4. The server asks: “Are you ready to order?” You need more time.
items.why: Just a minute, please is polite and clear.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.instr: Make it polite with “Could we have”:
ans: Could we have two waters, please?
items.model: Could we have two waters, please?
items.why: A full question is more polite than only the noun.

ans: What do you recommend, the fish or the pasta?
What do you recommend, the fish or the pasta
items.model: What do you recommend, the fish or the pasta?
items.why: What do you recommend + two options.

items.npc: Would you like something to drink?
items.why: Answer the question with the drink you want.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça uma versão mais informal.
group: Duplas resolvem e comparam.
Pontos por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: What do you recommend? · 2: I’ll have the soup, please. · 3: Could we have some bread? · 4: Just a minute, please.
Gap: have · have · Could we have two waters, please? · What do you recommend, the fish or the pasta? · Yes, a lemonade, please.
extra: Say each answer aloud with the strong words.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — a table for dinner

brief.teacher: You are the waiter (add a surprise during the scene!).
brief.student: You are the guest: get a recommendation, order and ask for one extra thing.

orders: Chicken with rice and a lemonade
Soup and a salad and water
complications: The dish you want is finished (“We’re out of that”).
The waiter brings the wrong drink.
You need more time to choose.
You don’t understand the menu word.
success: I order food and a drink.
I ask for one extra thing.

teach.goal: Simulação com surpresa e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Use o restaurante favorito do estudante.
Rodada 1 com chunks; 2 só palavras-chave; 3 sem roteiro.
Fale ~30%; anote 2–3 correções.
extra: What if the dish has meat and you are vegetarian?

errors.r: Is the chicken finished? / Do you still have the chicken?

support: Volte à rodada 1; só a primeira frase.
stretch: Peça para duas pessoas e pergunte o que vem com o prato.

rounds.title: Get advice
rounds.task: Guest asks for a recommendation. Waiter answers.
rounds.hint: What do you recommend? / The… is great.

rounds.title: Order
rounds.task: Order a dish and a drink.

rounds.title: Extras
rounds.task: Ask for two extra things for the table.

rounds.title: Share
rounds.task: Whole group: each pair says what they ordered.

infogap.title: Today’s menu
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Guest asks the waiter
a.task: You know the chicken and the salad. Ask about the rest.

b.title: Waiter answers
b.task: You know the fish and the dessert. Ask about the rest.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada.
Com 6 estudantes, 3 duplas simultâneas.
Cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
answers: Info gap: A tem Chicken $14 e Salad $6; B tem Fish $16 com batatas e Dessert apple pie $5.
extra: How much is the fish?
What is the dessert of the day?

errors.r: The fish is sixteen dollars. / It’s $16.

pages.title: Group mission — dinner at a restaurant
pages.goal: Each group must order a full dinner and solve one small problem — in English.

missions.mission: Ask for a recommendation. Order a main dish and a drink. The waiter says the dish is finished: choose another.
missions.constraint: Use “What do you recommend?” and “I’ll have…”

missions.mission: Your friend is late. Ask for water and one more menu. Order a soup.
You need more time. Then order a salad and a juice. Ask what comes with the salad.
missions.constraint: Use “Just a minute, please.” and “It comes with…?”

success: Ask for a recommendation or a detail.
Be polite from start to end.

teach.goal: Realizar algo: pedir um jantar e resolver um problema.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne garçom e cliente.
1ª rodada com frases de apoio; 2ª palavras-chave; 3ª sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
answers: Modelo: “What do you recommend?” → “The chicken is great.” → “I’ll have the chicken, please.”
extra: What if the waiter forgets your drink?
support: Dê o “Start with” de cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a restaurant to ask for a table for two tonight and ask what they recommend.
pages.model: Hi! **Could we have** a table for two tonight at 7:00? **What do you recommend** for dinner? Thank you very much!
checklist: I asked for a table (Could we have…?).
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação.
solo: Corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários.
group: Troquem os textos entre colegas.
extra: Add the day and the time.

errors.w: I want a table to two.
errors.r: Could we have a table for two?

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You asked for a recommendation and ordered clearly.
prompts.improve: Example: Stress the strong words: I’ll HAVE the CHICKen.
prompts.next: Example: Order for two people and handle a problem without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask the waiter for advice.

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: The waiter asks: “Are you ready to order?” You are ready. Order soup.
tasks.model: Yes. I’ll have the soup, please.

tasks.name: Use a new expression
tasks.prompt: Ask for some more bread for the table.
tasks.model: Could we have some more bread?

items: Record a 45–60 second audio ordering dinner.
Write a message to reserve a table for two.
Choose three expressions and write your own examples.
Listen to the dialogue again and find two expressions.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem anotações: pergunta, resposta e expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega.
answers: What do you recommend? · Yes. I’ll have the soup, please. · Could we have some more bread?
extra: Revisão espaçada: próxima aula, uma semana depois e na missão da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: I’ll have the chicken and a lemonade, please.
ladder.goal: Order and ask a simple question.

ladder.say: What do you recommend? I don’t eat meat, so I’d like something without it.
I’d like to know what comes with the fish, and whether it can be made without butter.
Would it be possible to swap the fries for a salad? I’m trying to eat lighter.
If the kitchen could manage it, I’d be delighted to have the sauce on the side.
ladder.goal: Make a request with elegant, polite register.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
